t: You're looking at La Mitrailleuse, an oil painting from 1915, which hangs at Tate Britain. It was painted by C. R. W. Nevinson, one of the most famous war artists of the First World War. He made it while on honeymoon leave from serving as an ambulance driver with the Royal Army Medical Corps on the Western Front. So this is a picture by someone who had seen the war at first hand, painted during a brief break from it.
